review_text_raw:
Been a backer since...Feb 2016.  It is very nice to see the end product, however long it took.  I liked it so far, and from other reviews, I am looking forward to the play time I will get since it is my type of game.  

Pros:
Unique puzzle type game
Engaging text based storyline (I'm looking at you, uncle)
Enough tutorial to get you started.

Cons:
Fair amount of bugs needed to be fixed
Log in animation seems pointless other than extending the transition.
Layout could use a little TLC.  Screen real estate takes a hit when you have the "prerequisites" list open and you're trying to look at the data.
NPC seems very linear, would have been nice to play with the morality of it all.  The person I am expecting to go against doesn't have to be rude to me, although what I am expecting now might be a different outcome.


Overall, a really cool game for the price.  A good bit of superficial bugs for something officially released since Oct 2018.  I am very happy to have backed it 3 years ago.

Edit 10/18/18:
Had to call this out: I posted a bug that broke my game onto the devs' Trello board, and they fixed it and patched it within a day! This is the kind of awesomeness I expect from game devs. Thank you guys for your hard work :)

I think I'm about halfway through with this game. It's very clear that Monomyth Games has put in a ton of time and effort into making this game really varied and fun. That being said, here are the major issues that I have with the game so far that make me closer to a "neutral" recommendation:

-UI is *very* clunky. Backing out of a profile or even trying to figure out how to end your very first day are both insanely unintuitive. This is fixable, and I have no doubt Monomyth is on it.

-Some weird prompts that have game-long consequences, but you have no idea at the time. For example, (mild spoiler) [spoiler] you get a text early on in the game asking if you used to like "Max" or "Serena" from high school. No indication at all that it's romantic, or that Max is a man. If you pick Max, you are now gay for the rest of the game. [/spoiler] Not anything major at all, but just... strange. 

-Doing "side by side" comparisons (i.e. "Try to find out the real profile, given these archived profiles of former criminals") are very hard to do, mainly because of the clunky UI. You can only have 1 profile at a time, and you can only save a certain amount of evidence to compare side-by-side at once. I wish you could have 2+ profiles open, especially since a lot of cases in the game require you to do side-by-side comparisons.

Regardless of these issues, if you're willing to have some patience for these developers, I still highly recommend the game. This game is basically "Papers, Please" but NSA-esque. You unlock more and more tools as you go along such as: [spoiler] social media posts, call metadata, audio recordings of calls, package tracking... you name it. [/spoiler]. As I said, it's very clear the company has put a ton of time into this game and want it to be fun.

review_text_raw:
I loved this game. Recommend.

Selling point:
The morally ambigious writing and the logical characters. The game makes you feel you are part of a 90s political thriller, set in the modern world.

Pros:
- writing is amazing
- puzzles are logical and set in the real world
- aesthetics are minimalistic, but cool (my only gripe is that some people looked bizarre),
- game duration (game changes pace once it gets slightly repetitive, which was welcome)
- world-building (despite its conspiracy context, the game is very much grounded in the real world both in terms of politics and technology, and everything felt contemporary, even in its future years)
- achievements (100% completion is based on completing the game, not on some wild goose chase)

Cons:
- UI (common visual glitches, although I do play on linux which may add glitches; animations are slow, changing suspects is slow, link puzzles between multiple suspects are slow not due to complexity of puzzle but due to UI problems; clicking on suspects is difficult even if you remove map scrolling)
- some puzzle solutions have obtuse or small consequences, could have kept its linearity but with some more impact on world, you do get some comics balloons for some optional objectives
- game does push you to become a government bot, even if your character disagrees wildly with that (but this is somewhat necessary from a writing standpoint).

In Brief:
This is a very good game for someone who is interested in mass surveillance, abuse of power, corporate capitalism, world politics, solving puzzles, and in general feeling like a special part of an important conspiracy.

review_text_raw: It's an alright entry in the dystopian sim category, but it really has a number of flaws. For one, besides "Oh no I don't get money today" there's almost no penalty for failure, and money itself is pretty irrelevant besides buying yourself new toys. There's no consequences! You can leave the org at multiple story points, which "ends" the game til you reload it. Most dystopian games make you feel like you have no choice in the matter of your participation, though the data selling portion does give you some of that "I have to be doing this" feel. It falls short in communicating clear directions sometimes, too; you get new tools and data given to you but sometimes the instructions get int he way of making accurate assessments.
